dossier.architecture: Hybrid under/over-bumper pickup and a shared shooting/climbing pivot.

subsystems.intake: Spring-out friction-driven collectors compress the note through limited bumper clearance; supplementary over-bumper intake.
subsystems.transfer: Sensor-tracked conveyor feeds a staged launcher.
subsystems.scoring: Pivoted launcher with matched wheel arrangement and revised output power for range.
subsystems.endgame: Ratcheting hooks capture chain; shooter wheels react against stage; flexible fingers open trap.
subsystems.controls: Front note-detection and rear target camera; distance-based speed/angle maps and automated note states.

versions: Timing-pulley intake prototype changed to inline friction drive for packaging. Launcher power increased after range limitations.
dossier.analysis: The friction drive is a packaging response, not a universal transmission preference. Shared launch/climb actuation also makes the reaction geometry and ratchet behavior central to trap reliability.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.

context_documents.title: 2024-2075 · Compliant bumper entry and a supported pivot solve separate uncertainties
context_documents.body:
# 2024-2075: Compliant bumper entry and a supported pivot solve separate uncertainties

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Spring-loaded under-bumper collector segments compress notes through a limited opening, with an additional over-bumper collector. A sensor-tracked conveyor stages the note. The launcher angle is driven on both sides, and the source describes protecting the separate position sensor/transmission from damage.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team connects the two-sided pivot drive to reducing wobble and describes launcher changes made to gain useful shooting distance. The independent collector segments are intended to acquire at a wall as well as in open space.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Compliant entry can increase tolerance while making the note’s shape and arrival speed variable. The downstream stage must restore a repeatable state before release. A symmetric pivot support helps angular repeatability, but the stiffness of the frame and belt/chain tension still determine the actual output angle.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure entry success at bumper contact, note deformation after transport, and left/right pivot deflection under acceleration. Verify stage sensing before comparing range.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/456972](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/456972)

source_reviews.title: Team 2075 Enigma Robotics Presents Masquerade
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team reveal and event updates.
facts: Reveal identifies a start-of-match intake release. Kentwood update reports intake robustness changes, LL3G, LED feedback, shuttling and automatic note pickup, and a climb redesign adding Trap. Team reported 9/12 successful qualification traps and 4/4 in eliminations at the Michigan state championship.
source_reviews.limitations: Team event report, not an independent match audit or a drawing set.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers — 2075 Enigma Robotics
source_reviews.locator: 1:18–2:10 intake views; 2:37–3:20 deck and panel; 3:50–5:10 head, side drives and Stage
source_reviews.review_basis: Visually inspected public storyboard frames at approximately five-second intervals.
facts: Shows distinct low and raised pickup views, underside intake sections, a clear deck and tall hinged assembly, opposing launch rollers, a side chain drive, and a suspended robot in match footage.
source_reviews.limitations: Caption requests returned HTTP 429. Sampling does not establish motor count, materials, or the speaker’s rationale for the pivot design.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Masquerade uses compact floor collection hardware at the bumper and a tall scoring assembly on a pivot. The photographs and interview frames distinguish a low acquisition arrangement from a raised roller position. Above a clear deck, the launch assembly presents two wheel rows at the end of a supported structure that can rotate relative to the base. The later event reports make endgame a meaningful part of the architecture. The team retained note pickup and Speaker/shuttle functionality while replacing the climb system and adding Trap between district events.
source_review.piece_flow: With the front of the robot tilted toward the camera, separated underside roller groups are visible beside the bumper. Other views show the green and gray roller spanning the front higher up. The clear deck sits below the entrance to the central upright mechanism, with a wide horizontal roller visible at the foot of its panel. That geometry is consistent with an inward handoff then elevation toward the launcher. The frames identify the contact regions, while the source does not establish the drive timing, exact note storage position, or how the note is routed for Trap. The team separately reports automatic note detection for pickup, which establishes a perception feature without identifying internal possession sensors.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The upper assembly is held between paired sides, with a prominent lateral chain and sprocket visible at one end. Keeping the launcher above the floor intake leaves room for a steep path while placing a substantial moving structure close to the front collector. The bumper and clear deck constrain where the note can enter. The match segment shows the endgame configuration changing the chassis attitude, so a pit pose alone cannot define the outlet location at the Stage.

subsystems.name: Floor pickup and higher roller assembly
subsystems.construction: Visible green and gray wheel groups on a transverse shaft; underside inspection frames expose multiple roller and support groups below the blue bumper.
subsystems.operation: Pickup hardware can be presented low or in a raised position. The team reveal identifies a separate start-of-match release action.
subsystems.team_rationale: The Kentwood update explicitly targeted reliability and robustness. Spring rate and wall pickup rationale were not verified in the primary material reviewed.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compliance would allow a narrow entry to accept differently worn rings, but if roller sections deflect unevenly the downstream handoff can arrive skewed.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper opening, first nip and clear deck must overlap at entry. The raised roller assembly also needs clearance from the central scoring frame.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: After front impact, test both sides and the center with a loaded note. Inspect release hardware and roller alignment as distinct checks.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact segmentation and spring arrangement, wall pickup envelope and as-built change details.

subsystems.name: Transfer and scoring pivot
subsystems.construction: A tall panel with a transverse roller at its foot is visible below opposing large launcher wheels. Close-ups show lateral sprocket and chain hardware.
subsystems.operation: The upper assembly changes pitch relative to the chassis. The team reported a dedicated shuttling mode and automatic pickup.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team update records the functions. The reason for two-sided drive and any protected feedback transmission still needs primary confirmation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A two-sided support can resist twist only if the frame remains square and transmission loads stay balanced. A narrow beam condition can confirm occupancy while missing a skewed rim.
subsystems.interfaces: Lower pickup must hand off across the base of the panel. Pivot position governs the launch direction and alters adjacent clearances.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check for side-to-side lash and clear-deck interference at loaded angle limits. Recheck sensing after chain tension changes.
subsystems.unknowns: Feeder timing, shot settings and exact pivot motor and encoder topology.

subsystems.name: Climb, Trap and controls
subsystems.construction: Visible upright structure and a field segment with the chassis suspended. Team reported a complete climb redesign plus LED and LL3G changes.
subsystems.operation: Michigan state results demonstrate repeated Trap use as reported by the team. The team tuned pickup and localization before that event.
subsystems.team_rationale: The update gives timing and capability changes but does not specify why each climb part was replaced.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A stable chain-supported pose is required for a repeatable Trap delivery. Success counts do not isolate hook engagement from note delivery failures.
subsystems.interfaces: The suspended base, scoring structure and Trap opening must line up under load. Vision and feedback changes affect acquisition and approach independently.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check hook capture and Trap placement separately. A Kentwood roboRIO failure required replacement; the post does not establish its cause.
subsystems.unknowns: Actuator, hook linkage, shared pivot load path and measured Trap repeatability by failure category.

revisions: March reveal establishes the intake deployment baseline. By Kentwood the team reported intake work, vision and feedback changes, shuttling, pickup detection and a new climb with Trap. Before state it tuned localization and pickup.
transferable_principles: Document both entrance geometries with a note present and confirm they converge on a common staged pose.
Track chain engagement, stable hang and successful deposit as separate stages.
disconfirming_conditions: A raised roller might primarily aid a distinct acquisition pose, so visual similarity cannot establish shared drive.
If the climb loads enter a separate frame, shooter-to-climber coupling inferred from nearby hardware would be overstated.
remaining_gaps: No primary verbal transcript, pivot wiring or spring specifications were recovered.
